title: Maximum Number of Items From Sale I
summary: Given a 2D integer array items, where each item is represented as [factori, pricei], and an integer budget, determine the maximum total number of item copies (both purchased and free) you can obtain.
statement: Given a 2D integer array items, where each item is represented as [factori, pricei], and an integer budget, determine the maximum total number of item copies (both purchased and free) you can obtain. You can purchase any number of copies of any items as long as the total cost does not exceed the budget. For each item you purchase, you will receive one free copy of every other item whose factor is divisible by the factor of the purchased item, but only once per item type. The objective is to maximize the total number of items you can obtain.
constraints: Each item type is [factor,price], and budget is nonnegative.
The first promotional purchase of a type also yields one free copy of every type whose factor is divisible by it; later purchases still yield the bought copy.
Maximize total purchased and free copies.
hints: Each promotion is available at most once, which is a 0/1 knapsack choice.
Its reward is the number of factors divisible by the purchased factor.
Update budget states backward, then spend each leftover amount on the globally cheapest ordinary copy.
Every plan separates uniquely into first promotional purchases and nonpromotional repeat purchases.
editorial: Every plan separates uniquely into first promotional purchases and nonpromotional repeat purchases.

tests.explanation: Choosing promotions and spending the remainder on the cheapest type yields four items.
One promotion plus two further copies obtains three items.
